page_content.about:
CasSpeed is a free, open-source alternative to commercial speed test sites for home users, network administrators, and developers. It measures download and upload throughput, latency, jitter, and packet loss without advertisements or tracking.

You can run a test anonymously. Registered users can keep history, associate tests with named devices, and use API tokens for automation. Results stay private unless their owner explicitly creates a share link.

The product has no paid feature gates and does not require an external testing API. Source code and documentation are available at [GitHub](https://github.com/webappsgo/casspeed).
page_content.privacy:
This CasSpeed service is operated by the organization that installed it. The operator controls service availability and server-side retention settings.

Speed tests store measurement results, a one-way hash of the client IP address, and the user agent. The application does not store the plain client IP address. Anonymous results are retained for {retention}. Account history remains until the user deletes it or the account is removed.

Unshared results are visible only to the originating anonymous browser session or the account that owns them. A result becomes public only after its owner explicitly creates a share link. A shared result contains measurements and does not disclose the plain IP address or user agent.

Account profile details, devices, and API tokens are private to their owner. Raw API tokens are shown once at creation and stored as SHA-256 hashes. Contact the service operator for privacy requests.
page_content.terms: Use CasSpeed only to measure networks you are authorized to use. Do not use the service to disrupt its operation, evade access controls, or submit harmful content. The service is provided by its operator, who controls availability, retention, and applicable terms.
page_content.help:
Choose **Start speed test** on the [home page](/). The test measures latency, download speed, and upload speed using this CasSpeed server. Keep the page open while the test runs.

Unshared results remain private to the browser session that started the test. Choose **Share result** to create a public link. Registered users can sign in to keep history and manage devices and API tokens.

### API quick start

Start a test with `POST /api/v1/speed-tests`. The response includes an `id`; connect to `GET /api/v1/speed-tests/{id}/status` for live updates. Retrieve an owned result with `GET /api/v1/speed-tests/{id}`. See the [API reference](/server/docs/swagger) for the API contract.

### API documentation

- [Swagger UI](/server/docs/swagger) explores REST operations.
- [GraphiQL](/server/docs/graphql) runs read-only queries for public health, your own results, and shared results.
- [MCP server](/server/help/mcp) makes API operations available to configured MCP clients.

For machine use, send a bearer API token in the `Authorization` header. Never place tokens in a URL or share them in logs. MCP clients use the same API token.
page_content.help_mcp:
CasSpeed exposes a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `/api/v1/server/mcp`, with direct aliases at `/api/mcp` and `/mcp`. The endpoint accepts JSON-RPC over HTTP POST and requires the same `Authorization: Bearer …` API token used by the REST API.

Configure your MCP client to use the endpoint URL and a dedicated, revocable API token. Keep the token secret. The MCP transport uses protocol revision `2026-07-28`; clients must send `MCP-Protocol-Version` and `Mcp-Method` headers that match the JSON-RPC request metadata.

MCP operations must enforce the same ownership and permissions as the matching API operations.
page_content.security_policy: Please report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the service operator. Allow reasonable time for investigation and remediation before public disclosure. Do not access, modify, or retain other users' data.
page_content.security_thanks: No security acknowledgements have been published.
